mechanism_claims.claim_text: Hp1404 analogues are supported as LPS-interacting antibacterial peptides by LPS competition assays and CD spectra; Hp1404-T1e shows stronger LPS-sensitive activity than the parent peptide.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: Hp1404-T1c, Hp1404-T1d, Hp1404-T1e, and Hp1404 where compared
direct_assay_types: LPS competition antimicrobial assay at 1x/2x MIC
mechanism_claims.limitations: Exact figure-curve values are not tabulated in local text; the claim is limited to source-described assay effects and figure-located evidence.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The paper directly assays bacterial membrane perturbation by calcein leakage, NPN uptake, cytoplasmic membrane depolarization, and PI uptake; Hp1404 is stronger in calcein leakage whereas Hp1404-T1e remains active through membrane and intracellular mechanisms.

mechanism_claims.limitations: Figure-only curves are not over-quantified beyond values reported in the source text.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Hp1404-T1d and Hp1404-T1e have direct DNA-binding evidence from gel retardation experiments, supporting a possible intracellular component for their antibacterial mechanism.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: Hp1404-T1d and Hp1404-T1e, with Buforin 2 and other peptides as controls/comparators
mechanism_claims.limitations: The paper frames DNA interaction as possible mechanism support; it is not generalized to all Hp1404 analogues.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Antibiofilm activity is directly supported by MBIC Table 4 and live/dead biofilm imaging, with Hp1404-T1e among the strongest peptide rows across tested P. aeruginosa strains.
mechanism_claims.limitations: This is retained as antibiofilm phenotype evidence, not as proof of a quorum-specific molecular target.
